generation.explanation: When you scale a triangle by a factor k, every linear length—including its base and height—is multiplied by k. Area equals ½ × base × height, so the new area becomes ½ × (k·base) × (k·height) = k² times the original area. The same k² rule holds for any 2D shape because area is a product of two lengths.
